whenToUse: A virtualenv or exported variable seems to vanish between commands

questions.stem: In a Python project, Claude ran `source .venv/bin/activate` in one Bash command, but its next `pytest` call fails with missing modules. The developer wants every Bash command in the session to use the virtualenv, with the least setup. What should they do?

options.text: Activate the virtualenv before launching Claude Code
options.why: The docs recommend activating it before launch so every command inherits it.

options.text: Add "always activate .venv" to CLAUDE.md
options.why: It's guidance only; each command still runs in its own process.

options.text: Set `CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1`
options.why: It controls directory carry-over, not environment variables.

options.text: Raise `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`
options.why: The failure is a missing environment, not a timeout.

questions.explanation: Each Bash command runs in a separate process, so an activation in one command is gone in the next. Activating the virtualenv before launching Claude Code is the documented, zero-config fix. Writing the rule in CLAUDE.md is tempting, but it only guides Claude and still depends on it activating in every command.
keywordCues: every Bash command in the session

options.text: Activar el virtualenv antes de lanzar Claude Code

options.text: Poner `CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1`

options.text: Subir `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`
options.why: La falla es un entorno faltante, no un timeout.

es.explanation: Cada comando Bash corre en un proceso aparte, así que una activación en un comando desaparece en el siguiente. Activar el virtualenv antes de lanzar Claude Code es la solución documentada y sin configuración. Escribirlo en CLAUDE.md tienta, pero solo guía a Claude y depende de que active en cada comando.

questions.stem: A team needs a short-lived token, computed when each session starts, available as an environment variable to every Bash command Claude runs. It must happen automatically in every session, not depend on Claude remembering. Which setup fits?

options.text: Have Claude `export` the token in its first command
options.why: Exported variables don't persist to the next Bash command.

options.text: A SessionStart hook that populates `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`
options.why: The hook runs at every session start, and the file's exports apply before each Bash command.

options.text: Instructions in CLAUDE.md to fetch the token first
options.why: It depends on Claude following guidance, and exports still wouldn't persist.

options.text: Run the token command with `run_in_background: true`
options.why: A background task doesn't share environment variables with later commands.

questions.explanation: Environment variables don't persist between Bash commands because each runs in a separate process. `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` points to a script whose exports run before each Bash command, and a SessionStart hook can populate it dynamically when the session starts. Exporting in the first command is the tempting shortcut, but the variable is gone by the next call.

es.stem: Un equipo necesita un token de corta vida, calculado al iniciar cada sesión, disponible como variable de entorno para todo comando Bash que corra Claude. Debe ocurrir automáticamente en cada sesión, sin depender de que Claude lo recuerde. ¿Qué configuración sirve?

options.text: Que Claude haga `export` del token en su primer comando
options.why: Las variables exportadas no persisten al siguiente comando Bash.

options.text: Un hook SessionStart que llene `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`
options.why: El hook corre al iniciar cada sesión, y los exports del archivo aplican antes de cada comando Bash.

options.text: Instrucciones en CLAUDE.md para traer el token primero
options.why: Depende de que Claude siga la guía, y los exports igual no persistirían.

options.text: Correr el comando del token con `run_in_background: true`
options.why: Una tarea en segundo plano no comparte variables de entorno con comandos posteriores.

es.explanation: Las variables de entorno no persisten entre comandos Bash porque cada uno corre en un proceso aparte. `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` apunta a un script cuyos exports corren antes de cada comando Bash, y un hook SessionStart puede llenarlo dinámicamente al iniciar la sesión. Exportar en el primer comando es el atajo tentador, pero la variable desaparece en la siguiente llamada.

questions.stem: A project's full test suite takes about six minutes, and no timeout variables have been changed. The developer asks Claude to run it and wants to know what to expect. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)

options.text: Claude can pass a `timeout` longer than two minutes, up to ten
options.why: Claude sets the timeout parameter; the default ceiling is ten minutes.

options.text: If the timeout is reached, the command moves to the background
options.why: Claude Code backgrounds a timed-out command instead of stopping it, unless it starts with sleep.

options.text: The developer must set a per-command timeout in the prompt
options.why: You never set a per-command timeout; Claude manages it.

options.text: The default timeout is already ten minutes
options.why: The default is two minutes; ten is the default ceiling.

options.text: Any command over two minutes is killed
options.why: Claude can request more, and a timed-out command moves to the background.

questions.explanation: `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` applies when Claude passes no timeout and is two minutes out of the box, while `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` caps what Claude may request at ten minutes. Claude passes the `timeout` parameter itself, so a six-minute suite fits under the ceiling. If a command still reaches its timeout, Claude Code moves it to the background rather than stopping it.
keywordCues: no timeout variables have been changed

es.stem: La suite completa de tests de un proyecto tarda unos seis minutos, y no se cambió ninguna variable de timeout. El desarrollador pide a Claude correrla y quiere saber qué esperar. ¿Qué dos afirmaciones son correctas? (Elige dos.)

options.text: Claude puede pasar un `timeout` mayor a dos minutos, hasta diez
options.why: Claude fija el parámetro timeout; el techo por defecto es diez minutos.

options.text: Si se alcanza el timeout, el comando pasa a segundo plano
options.why: Claude Code pasa a segundo plano un comando vencido en vez de detenerlo, salvo que empiece con sleep.

options.text: El desarrollador debe fijar un timeout por comando en el prompt
options.why: Tú nunca fijas un timeout por comando; Claude lo gestiona.

options.text: El timeout por defecto ya es diez minutos
options.why: El valor por defecto es dos minutos; diez es el techo por defecto.

options.text: Todo comando de más de dos minutos se mata
options.why: Claude puede pedir más, y un comando vencido pasa a segundo plano.

es.explanation: `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` aplica cuando Claude no pasa timeout y vale dos minutos por defecto, mientras que `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` limita lo que Claude puede pedir a diez minutos. Claude pasa el parámetro `timeout` por sí mismo, así que una suite de seis minutos cabe bajo el techo. Si igual llega al timeout, Claude Code la pasa a segundo plano en vez de detenerla.

questions.stem: Which environment variable points to a shell script that Claude Code runs before each Bash command, so its exports persist?

options.text: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE

questions.explanation: `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is the path to a shell script whose contents Claude Code runs before each Bash command in the same shell process, so its exports are visible. Set it before launching Claude Code, or let a SessionStart hook populate it dynamically.

es.stem: ¿Qué variable de entorno apunta a un script de shell que Claude Code corre antes de cada comando Bash, para que sus exports persistan?

options.text: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE

es.explanation: `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` es la ruta a un script de shell cuyo contenido Claude Code corre antes de cada comando Bash en el mismo proceso, así que sus exports se ven. Fíjala antes de lanzar Claude Code o deja que un hook SessionStart la llene dinámicamente.

questions.stem: Claude started a dev server with `run_in_background: true`. Which slash command lists and stops background tasks?

options.text: /tasks
/bashes

questions.explanation: Background commands keep running while Claude works. `/tasks` lists them and lets you stop one, after which Claude moves on instead of waiting for it.

es.stem: Claude levantó un dev server con `run_in_background: true`. ¿Qué comando de barra lista y detiene las tareas en segundo plano?

options.text: /tasks
/bashes

es.explanation: Los comandos en segundo plano siguen corriendo mientras Claude trabaja. `/tasks` los lista y te deja detener uno, tras lo cual Claude sigue en vez de esperarlo.

recall.prompt: Explain what carries over between Claude's Bash commands and what doesn't, and how to make environment variables persist.
recall.promptEs: Explica qué se mantiene entre los comandos Bash de Claude y qué no, y cómo hacer que las variables de entorno persistan.
recall.idealAnswer: Each Bash command runs in a separate process. A cd carries over while it stays inside the project or an added directory, but exported variables don't. To persist variables, set CLAUDE_ENV_FILE to a script before launching, use a SessionStart hook to populate it, or activate the virtualenv before starting Claude Code.
rubric: Each command is a separate process
cd inside the project carries over

recall.prompt: A teammate suggests having Claude run `export AWS_PROFILE=dev` as its first Bash step each session. Why won't later commands see it, and what fits instead?
recall.promptEs: Un compañero sugiere que Claude corra `export AWS_PROFILE=dev` como primer paso Bash de cada sesión. ¿Por qué no lo verán los comandos siguientes y qué sirve en su lugar?
recall.idealAnswer: Each Bash command runs in its own process, so an export in one command is not available in the next. Put the export in a script referenced by CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, which runs before each Bash command, or populate that file from a SessionStart hook.
rubric: Use CLAUDE_ENV_FILE or a SessionStart hook
